newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Shell Venezuela sees 70,000 bpd in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Shell Venezuela sees 70,000 bpd in 1997.

text.p: Shell Venezuela plans to more than double its oil output to 70,000 barrels per day (bpd) by the end of this year, company president Bernard Wheelahan told journalists on Tuesday.

He said current production from the Urdaneta West field stood at 30,000 bpd after $550 million investment, and the company planned to invest $1 billion in the field by the year 2000 when output was expected to reach 100,000 bpd.
The field is operated by Shell under a contract with state- owned Petroleos de Venezuela in return for a fixed per-barrel fee and capital expenditure recovery.
Wheelahan said Shell had studied all the fields offered in Venezuela's upcoming third round of operating licences and expected to receive contract details this week.
